questions.prompt: How do Regions and Availability Zones relate?

options.text: A Region contains multiple Availability Zones
An Availability Zone contains multiple Regions
They are two words for the same thing
A Region is a single data center inside an AZ

questions.explanation: A Region is an isolated geographic area that contains multiple Availability Zones; each AZ is one or more isolated data centers within that Region.

questions.prompt: Why should a production workload run in more than one Availability Zone?

options.text: It makes the app run a different programming language
AZs fail independently, so multiple AZs remove the single point of failure
AWS charges less for using more AZs
A single AZ cannot run more than one server

questions.explanation: Availability Zones are isolated and fail independently, so spreading a workload across two or more keeps it available even if one AZ has an outage.

questions.prompt: Which services are GLOBAL rather than Regional? Select all that apply.

options.text: IAM
Amazon Route 53
Amazon EC2
Amazon CloudFront

questions.explanation: IAM, Route 53, and CloudFront are global. EC2 is Regional — an instance lives in one Region and AZ.

questions.prompt: AWS sites that cache content close to users for CloudFront (rather than running your servers) are called ____ locations.
questions.explanation: Edge locations cache and deliver content near users for CloudFront and answer DNS for Route 53; they do not host your compute.

questions.prompt: Which factors should drive your choice of Region? Select all that apply.

options.text: Latency to your users
Cost, which varies by Region
Compliance / data-residency requirements
Whether the service is available in that Region

questions.explanation: All four matter: pick a Region near your users, mind that prices differ by Region, respect data-residency law, and confirm the service exists there.

questions.prompt: You store backups only in us-east-1. Are they automatically copied to another Region for safety?

options.text: Yes, AWS mirrors all data across Regions by default
No — Regions are isolated; cross-Region replication must be configured on purpose
Yes, but only for S3
Only if the backup is larger than 5 TB

questions.explanation: Regions are isolated and data stays put by default. Any cross-Region copy for disaster recovery is something you must set up yourself.
